messages.subject: spde prior specification
parts: In spde approach how can i define my own priors for parameters? is that possible with control.family for all kind of parameter like coefficient and hyper parameters?

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] spde prior specification
parts:
In principle, yes, you can supply any prior specification for the spde parameters via the hyper parameter of the f() function. If you just want to set the parameters of the multivariate normal prior (spde2.matern) or pcprior (spde2.pcmatern), you can do that when constructing the spde object, using spde2.matern/pcmatern. Do you have som other prior in mind?

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: spde prior specification
parts:
Please see the examples in the documentation of the priors at
http://www.r-inla.org/models/priors
as well as
?control.fixed

For f()-models, f(..., hyper=list())
For the observation likelihood, inla(..., control.family=list(hyper=...))
For fixed effects, inla(..., control.fixed=list(prec=...))

Finn

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: spde prior specification
parts:
The most generic model input mechanism is... rgeneric (see inla.doc("rgeneric") and demo(rgeneric)).

With this you can define any random effect and any prior. The problem is that you have to make the "right" and "smart" choices to make the model work well. You have to know the "practical theory" behind INLA.

I would not use this to put an arbitrary prior on fixed effects. For this I would use model="iid" and change the hyper-prior on that model. (Here, every observation would have the same iid effect, but be weighted by the covariate value).

Kind regards,
Haakon
